tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

content.text:
One quick flag before the findings: the Contentful/docs agent's raw output tripped the harness's prompt-injection heuristic (tagged `settings-json`), which auto-neutralized any control-like characters before I saw it. I read the full output and found nothing instruction-shaped directed at me — just quoted doc/schema text — so I treated it as data and verified the load-bearing claims myself below rather than taking the agent's word for it. Likely source is `.docs/temp/SFCC-52-global-header-plan.md`, a raw 1445-line dev session log that may contain pasted JSON/tool-output blocks; say the word if you want me to pin down exactly which line tripped it.

## Headline

The three pieces don't combine the way you'd expect from the base SFCC template, and don't match what `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` currently says. **The mega menu is 100% Contentful-authored. SFCC Business Manager categories are fetched but completely unused for nav** — that's a deliberate, already-made decision that the docs never caught up with.

## How it actually works

```
_app/index.tsx
  useCategory() ──► SFCC category tree ──► passed as root/itemsKey/itemsCountKey props
                                             to <DrawerMenu> and <ListMenu>
                                             ┊
                                             ┊  IGNORED (see below)
                                             ▼
Contentful                                 useHeaderNav()
  headerNavigation                           │
   └─ headerNavItem[]  ◄──── getEntries ─────┘  (useContentfulClient, content_type:
       ├─ href (direct link)                     'headerNavigation', locale-aware)
       ├─ columns[] ──► navGroup                  │
       │                 ├─ heading                │
       │                 └─ link[] (label + free-text href)
       ├─ promoImage ──► image                     │
       └─ regions ──► region (siteId = SFCC site)  ▼
                                          ListMenuView / DrawerMenuView
                                          → MegaMenuContent (desktop) via toMegaMenuItem()
                                          → drawer L1→L2 drill-down (mobile)
```

**Confirmed directly** (I read these myself, not just via the research agents):
- [`_app/index.tsx:161-164`](overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx:161) fetches the SFCC category tree and passes it at [:432-436](overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx:432) (`DrawerMenu`) and [:441-445](overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx:441) (`ListMenu`).
- [`list-menu.tsx:148-156`](overrides/app/components/list-menu/list-menu.tsx:148)'s own JSDoc says it straight: those props are "accepted only for call-site compatibility with base `_app.jsx`'s SFCC category-tree contract... all of these are ignored except `maxColumns`." The container ([:164-168](overrides/app/components/list-menu/list-menu.tsx:164)) calls `useHeaderNav()` instead. `drawer-menu/index.tsx` mirrors this same pattern per the research trace.
- [`useHeaderNav.ts`](overrides/app/hooks/useHeaderNav.ts) — the real nav hook (not `use-navigation.ts`, which is a Tier-1-frozen, unrelated vendor `navigate()` wrapper) — queries Contentful directly via `useContentfulClient`, never touches `commerce-sdk-react`. Its query key and Contentful request both include `locale` ([:56](overrides/app/hooks/useHeaderNav.ts:56), [:67](overrides/app/hooks/useHeaderNav.ts:67)) — a locale-staleness bug noted in old planning notes is **not** present in the current code.
- Contentful schema (`scripts/contentful/content-types/`): `headerNavItem.href`/`link.href` are **free-text strings** — an editor manually pastes the destination URL. No field anywhere references an SFCC category ID.

**Why BM plays no role, not just "doesn't currently":** a planning log (`.docs/temp/SFCC-52-global-header-plan.md`, ~lines 1041-1047) shows the original tickets (SFCC-96/746/28) specified a BM-category-driven or hybrid model, and the team explicitly rejected it in favor of full Contentful ownership — including subcategory links — during planning.

## The gap worth knowing about

input.prompt:
Context: Zimmermann Salesforce PWA Kit (/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa). An investigation into the mega menu / global nav confirmed the following as-built architecture: the desktop mega menu (`overrides/app/components/list-menu/`) and mobile drawer nav (`overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/`) both fetch their data exclusively from Contentful via `overrides/app/hooks/useHeaderNav.ts` (content type `headerNavigation` → `headerNavItem[]` → `navGroup`/`link`, with `link.href` a free-text string). The SFCC category tree that `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx` still fetches via `useCategory()` and passes down as `root`/`itemsKey`/`itemsCountKey` props is explicitly ignored by both components — confirmed directly by reading `list-menu/list-menu.tsx:148-168`, whose own `ListMenuProps` JSDoc says those props are "accepted only for call-site compatibility with base `_app.jsx`'s SFCC category-tree contract... all of these are ignored except `maxColumns`."

This was a deliberate decision: a planning session log at `.docs/temp/SFCC-52-global-header-plan.md` (~lines 1041-1047) shows the original tickets (SFCC-96, SFCC-746, SFCC-28) specified a BM-category-tree-driven or hybrid model, and the team explicitly rejected that in favour of "full Contentful replacement everywhere, including subcategory links" during planning.

The problem: the confirmed documentation was never updated to reflect this decision, so it actively misleads anyone who reads it instead of the code:

1. **`.docs/integration/02-contentful.md`** — §1's content-ownership table (around line 33) lists `Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | Pending`. This should be updated to reflect that Contentful owns the entire nav tree (labels, links, columns, images), not just promotional tiles, and that this is settled, not Pending. §10's open item #2 (around lines 133-136) makes the same "Pending... working assumption is in the ownership table" statement and should be resolved/removed or rewritten to record the actual decision and cite `.docs/temp/SFCC-52-global-header-plan.md` as the source.

2. **`.docs/temp/openItems.md`** (around lines 51-53) — repeats the same stale "SFCC category tree + Contentful promo tiles" framing. Update or remove this item to match.

3. **`.docs/memory/projectState.md`** (last updated 2026-08-24) — doesn't mention the SFCC-52/746/96/97 mega-menu/nav work at all despite it running through 2026-08-31. Add an entry recording that the header/mega-menu/drawer nav is built and Contentful-driven (per this investigation). Also check its existing line noting "the mobile hamburger drawer has zero category navigation links" (around lines 79-82, under an SFCC-751 entry) — this is very likely superseded by the drawer nav build (`drawer-menu/index.tsx` now drills L1→L2 using Contentful-sourced items) and should be confirmed/retracted if so, rather than left contradicting the newer work.

4. **Stale code comments** — three files still say the mega-menu/drawer "isn't wired to any real state," dated to commit `ee9f1f23` (2026-08-27), but the wiring landed in the very next commits on the same branch (SFCC-96 commits `d9a064bb7`/`2b42527ab`, SFCC-97 commits `a2a687ae5`/`82f12cb6`): `overrides/app/components/header/headerTypes.ts:17-21`, `overrides/app/components/header/leftBar/index.tsx:16-19,21-22`, `overrides/app/components/header/rightBar/index.tsx:133-138,140-141`. Update these comments to reflect that `header/index.tsx` now derives and passes a real `menuExpanded` value (see `header/index.tsx:164-211`).

5. **`scripts/contentful/content-types/headerNavItem.js:29-31`** — comment claims `navGroup` "is authored on a separate branch... and has no local file in this content-types/ directory yet." This is false now — `navGroup.js` exists in the same directory (it was merged, unifying the old `footerNavGroup` type). Fix the comment.

Notes on file tiers (per `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md`): the `.docs/` files are not tier-classified at all, safe to edit directly. `scripts/contentful/content-types/` is Tier 2 (owner: Integration/SI Partner — notify before changing), but this is a comment-only fix with no schema/behavior change. The three header component files are Tier 2 "Global Shell" (owner: Both Squads — coordinate before touching), also comment-only. Follow this repo's AGENTS.md workflow (clarify → plan → implement) and its Doc integrity rule — since `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` is a confirmed integration doc, treat correcting it as flagging-and-fixing a doc/reality conflict per that rule, not a silent edit; a short note in the PR description calling out what changed and why (citing this investigation) is appropriate.

content.text:
**Short answer:** Everything shown in the mega menu — labels, links, columns, the promo image — comes from Contentful. Nothing is sourced from SFCC/Business Manager categories.

**The actual source chain, in Contentful:**

```
headerNavigation          (one root entry per locale, optionally more per region/storefront)
 └─ items[]  →  headerNavItem     (one per top-level nav label, e.g. "Clothing", "Z.Immerse")
                 ├─ href           → set only if it's a plain link, no dropdown
                 ├─ columns[]  →  navGroup     → set if it's a mega-menu trigger (1+ columns)
                 │                  ├─ heading        (optional column heading)
                 │                  └─ links[]  →  link
                 │                                   ├─ label
                 │                                   └─ href   ← plain text URL, editor types it in
                 ├─ promoImage    → image entry (the banner picture in the flyout)
                 └─ regions[]     → which storefronts this item applies to
```

So a content editor goes into Contentful, opens (or creates) a `Header Navigation` entry, and edits the `Header Nav Item`/`Nav Group`/`Link` entries it references. That's the entire content model — there's no field anywhere that points at an SFCC category ID.

**How the frontend gets it:** `overrides/app/hooks/useHeaderNav.ts` queries Contentful directly for the `headerNavigation` content type, picks the entry that matches the current storefront/locale (via the `regions` scoping above), and hands the resolved item list to the menu/drawer components to render. That's it — one hook, one Contentful query, nothing else in the chain.

The SFCC category tree still gets fetched elsewhere (`_app/index.tsx`) and passed toward the menu components as leftover plumbing from the base template, but — as covered last time — neither component reads it. It's fetched, then ignored.

content.content:
5:Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.
10:- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
11:- Live preview in Contentful Studio
13:- Contentful Studio Experiences — drag-and-drop page composition by editors
19:- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
22:**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).
27:| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
31:| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
32:| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
41:- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
54:        │        Editor preview only. Token set in MRT as an env var
71:- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
73:- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the `/preview` route renders the entry inside Studio's iframe. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK subscribes to `postMessage` events from Studio for real-time content updates. The CPA token is used client-side here — this is required by the SDK and is acceptable because: (a) the token is set only on dev/test/sit/uat (never staging or prod) MRT environments, (b) the route returns a 404 when no preview token is present, and (c) the route is `noindex`. The MRT proxy approach was considered but deferred in favour of the simpler client-side SDK integration.
94:| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
112:- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.
118:| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
120:| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |

content.text:
**Nowhere — it's manually typed in.** Contentful isn't pulling from SFCC, a spreadsheet, or any sync job for this content. A content editor logs into Contentful's web app and hand-creates/edits the entries directly. That's the whole "source."

Proof, not just inference:
- `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md:22`: *"SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial... Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio"* — editorial content in this project is authored by humans in Contentful's UI, full stop.
- I grepped every script under `scripts/contentful/` (`bootstrapSpace.mjs`, `seedRegions.mjs`, `seedLoginDrawerUiCopy.mjs`, `generateDefinitions.mjs`, `promoteAlias.mjs`, etc.) for any reference to `headerNavigation`/`headerNavItem`/`navGroup` — zero hits outside the schema definitions themselves. Two other content types *do* get programmatically seeded (`region` — makes sense, it's a fixed set of 8 storefronts; login-drawer UI copy) — nav content isn't one of them.
- The `link.href` field is a plain Symbol (short text) type in the schema, no relationship/validation to anything — someone literally pastes a URL string in.

**What that means practically:** if a nav link is ever wrong or pointing at a dead page, it's not a sync bug or a code bug — a human typed something wrong or a page moved and nobody updated the Contentful entry. There's no automated feed to fix or debug, and nothing in the pipeline validates the URL is real — you'd go straight into Contentful Studio and correct the entry by hand.
